statements.status_notes: The non-blocking (asynchronous) JSON parser in jackson-core does not enforce the maxNumberLength constraint of StreamReadConstraints (default 1000 characters). The async parsing path in NonBlockingUtf8JsonParserBase accumulates number digits into the TextBuffer without a length check and completes the token without calling the methods that validate integer and floating-point length. A JSON document with an arbitrarily long number supplied to an application that uses the async parser API causes unbounded allocation and an OutOfMemoryError, and a later getBigIntegerValue() or getDecimalValue() call adds quadratic BigInteger parsing time. The synchronous parsers enforce the limit correctly.
statements.impact_statement: Fixed in jackson-core 2.18.6 and 2.21.1. Every published Liquibase Secure image from 5.0.0 through 5.1.0 carries in-range copies, so this assessment does not rest on version: the core Liquibase Secure jar carries 2.20.0 in 5.0.x and 2.21.0 in 5.1.0, the license-tracking application in the 5.x ZIP carries 2.20.0 in 5.0.0 through 5.0.2, 2.20.1 in 5.0.3 and 2.21.0 in 5.1.0, and the AWS, Azure, BigQuery, Cassandra and Couchbase extensions carry copies between 2.17.2 and 2.21.0, with further copies relocated inside the Databricks and Snowflake JDBC drivers and the AWS SDK. The missing number-length check is only in the non-blocking parser, which Jackson creates only through JsonFactory.createNonBlockingByteArrayParser() or createNonBlockingByteBufferParser(). A bytecode scan of every class in every shipped jar, the license-tracking application included, found one caller outside Jackson itself: the Couchbase SDK's JsonStreamParser, bundled in the Couchbase extension from 5.1.0, which uses it to read query responses streamed from the configured Couchbase cluster. That input comes from the database the operator pointed Liquibase at, not from an untrusted party, and Liquibase does not rely on StreamReadConstraints as a security boundary (see the assessment of GHSA-2m67-wjpj-xhg9). Liquibase itself, the other extensions and the license-tracking application (Spring MVC, blocking parser) parse JSON only through the blocking parsers, which enforce the limit.

statements.status_notes: NumberInput.looksLikeValidNumber() in FasterXML jackson-core pre-validates stringified numbers with two regular expressions: PATTERN_FLOAT, present since 2.17.0, and PATTERN_FLOAT_TRAILING_DOT, added in 2.17.2. PATTERN_FLOAT places adjacent quantifiers over the same character class so input that ultimately fails to match forces Java's backtracking engine to retry every possible split point of the digit run. Matching cost therefore grows with the square of the input length. An attacker who can supply JSON that an application deserializes into a numeric target type reaches this method through jackson-databind's default String-to-number coercion for BigDecimal, BigInteger, Double and Float, and a small number of concurrent requests can exhaust a server's request-handling thread pool. The fix replaces both regular expressions with a hand-rolled single-pass scan.
statements.impact_statement: Fixed in jackson-core 2.18.11, 2.21.7 and 2.22.3. Every published Liquibase Secure image from 5.0.0 through 6.0.0 carries in-range copies, so this assessment does not rest on version. The copies were read from the version class of each copy in the shipped jars, including the obfuscated copy inside the core Liquibase Secure jar and copies relocated inside vendor drivers. In 6.0.0 the first-party copies are 2.22.2, the Couchbase SDK copy is 2.21.6, the snowflake-jdbc copy is 2.18.10 and the databricks-jdbc copy is 2.18.8; earlier releases carry older in-range copies. The vulnerable regular expression runs only when jackson-databind coerces a JSON string into a Float, Double, Number or BigDecimal target. A bytecode scan of every shipped jar found looksLikeValidNumber() called only by those jackson-databind number deserializers. Every Jackson binding call in Liquibase Secure's own code, including the changelog, snapshot, import-file, checks and license parsers, targets JsonNode trees, Object, Map or List of Map, where JSON strings stay strings and are never coerced. The license-tracking application in the 5.x ZIP binds request bodies whose fields are strings, string maps, whole numbers, booleans and dates only. The relocated vendor copies are private to their drivers and parse responses from the database service.

statements.status_notes: UTF8DataInputJsonParser._reportInvalidToken() in FasterXML jackson-core builds the offending-token text for its error message by appending Java identifier characters to a StringBuilder in a loop that has no upper bound. Unlike sibling parser implementations, it never consults ErrorReportConfiguration.getMaxErrorTokenLength(). A malformed token supplied to a parser created through JsonFactory.createParser(DataInput) is therefore accumulated in full, which can drive the StringBuilder to many times the raw payload size and trigger OutOfMemoryError for the JVM. Releases before 2.8.0 do not contain the affected class.
statements.impact_statement: Fixed in jackson-core 2.18.11, 2.21.7 and 2.22.3. Every published Liquibase Secure image from 5.0.0 through 6.0.0 carries in-range copies, so this assessment does not rest on version. The copies were read from the version class of each copy in the shipped jars, including the obfuscated copy inside the core Liquibase Secure jar and copies relocated inside vendor drivers. In 6.0.0 the first-party copies are 2.22.2, the Couchbase SDK copy is 2.21.6, the snowflake-jdbc copy is 2.18.10 and the databricks-jdbc copy is 2.18.8; earlier releases carry older in-range copies. The unbounded error-token buffer is in UTF8DataInputJsonParser, which Jackson creates only for input supplied as a java.io.DataInput through createParser(DataInput), readValue(DataInput) or readTree(DataInput). A bytecode scan of every class in every shipped jar, first-party and vendor, including the license-tracking application in the 5.x ZIP, found no code outside Jackson itself that passes a DataInput to Jackson. Liquibase Secure parses JSON from streams, readers, strings and files, which use the other parser implementations that do enforce the error-token limit.

statements.status_notes: Jackson Core's async parser can accumulate excessively long digit sequences (~20,000x amplification of the intended maxNumberLength limit) when input is fed in small chunks without a terminator, weakening DoS protection for applications that rely on maxNumberLength.
statements.impact_statement: Incomplete fix for a prior number-length constraint bypass: Jackson's async/non-blocking parser (NonBlockingJsonParser / ByteArrayFeeder) silently buffers digit characters up to maxStringLength instead of enforcing maxNumberLength when input arrives in small chunks without a terminator byte. Found in jackson-core 2.22.0 bundled into liquibase-aws-extension.jar and liquibase-azure.jar. Both extensions are outbound clients that call AWS/Azure APIs and parse the responses those services return over TLS; neither extension's own code invokes Jackson's non-blocking parser API, and neither exposes a network-facing endpoint that accepts attacker-controlled JSON. Exploiting this would require an attacker already able to forge or MITM AWS/Azure API responses, at which point far more direct attacks are already available.
